_how_to_use: Copy this file, rename it per campaign, and fill it in. One rubric = one offer.
A rubric is a business judgement, so it lives here where a human can read and argue
Every list of titles is matched as a lowercase SUBSTRING of the title column, so
'partner' also matches 'Managing Partner'. Order the lists most-specific first.
First rule that matches wins, in this order: account_disqualifiers -> role_type_rules
Run `grade_fit.py --explain --rubric <this file>` to read it back in plain English.
name: my-campaign
campaign: One line: what we are selling, to whom. Write this properly — it is the thing every grade is relative to.

columns._comment: Map logical fields -> the actual column names in YOUR csv. Delete any you don't have.
columns.title: title

grades.A: Owns this exact problem by job description. Has budget language for it.
grades.B: Can decide, and there is no dedicated owner in the org to route around them.
grades.C: Right company and right function, but junior — or someone better is the entry point.
grades.D: Right company, wrong person. Different function, or an operating/back-office seat.

account_disqualifiers.match: substring of the company description that means wrong company
account_disqualifiers.reason: why that rules them out — this text lands in fit_reason, make it readable

_require_account_description: true = a row with no company-level evidence is graded E as unqualified. Set false if your list has no description column.

role_type_rules._comment: Only used if your list has a role_type column. Values are yours to define.

portfolio_co.reason: works at a portfolio/subsidiary, not the company we are selling to

back_office.reason: finance/compliance seat, not the buying function

owner_titles: head of <the function that owns your problem>
_decision_title_exclusions: Stops 'vice president' from matching the 'president' substring. Keep it.

small_account.note: small enough that the decision-maker handles this personally

default.reason: in scope, but the entry point is unclear from the title alone
